rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth view takes illa as waw: they abide as long as heaven and earth and for whatever additional duration God wills.
rows.anchor: أن " إلا " بمعنى الواو وإلا كان الكلام متناقضا والمعنى خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض وما شاء ربك من الزيادة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this because illa meaning waw is unestablished; al-Farrāʾ mentions it, but scholars weakened it, and it also denies that the duration phrase implies permanence.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكره الفراء لكنهم ضعفوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري وجماعة من التابعين
rows.claim: A sixth view identifies the wretched as sinful monotheists who enter Hell, then leave for Paradise; the exception covers their release and the happy group's prior time in Hell, so the same people are wretched there and happy in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ونسبوا هذا القول إلى ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي سعيد الخدري من الصحابة وجماعة من التابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context divides all people gathered for Judgment into two groups, and the clauses beginning with أما explain those same exhaustive groups; they cannot mean only selected sinners and former sinners.
rows.anchor: مبدوين بأما التفصيلية مسوقان لتفصيل ما أجمل في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recasting the initial division as a special group leaves the general context unexplained and makes the doubled subjects, durations, and exceptions confusing and needlessly complex.
rows.anchor: السياق الظاهر في وصف أهل الجمع عامة لا يساعد على إرادة طائفة خاصة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī formulates the extraction view generally: all the gathered divide into Hell's wretched and Paradise's happy, while both exceptions concern sinful monotheists removed from Hell to Paradise; this avoids most earlier objections.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يقرر هذا الوجه على وجه التعميم بأن يقال المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh view says the will clause reinforces endless abiding: God will never will their departure, so the exception does not shorten their stay; it protects permanence from any cause except God's will.
rows.anchor: إن التعليق بالمشيئة إنما هو على سبيل التأكيد للخلود والتبعيد للخروج لأن الله سبحانه لا يشاء إلا خلودهم على ما حكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the seventh view lacks evidence that God will never will an end; the unsevered gift may suggest this for Paradise, but 11:107's statement that God does what He wills does not and may imply the opposite.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو وجه الضعف فيه فإن قوله ولن يشاء أصلا.

rows.speaker: سلام بن المستنير البصري
rows.claim: An eighth view makes the exception the time difference between successive groups entering Hell or Paradise, as groups are led in procession.
rows.anchor: ونقل الوجه عن سلام بن المستنير البصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording describes the duration of residence by its endpoint, not its start; everyone begins settling in Hell or Paradise on Judgment Day, so staggered arrivals do not explain the exception.
rows.anchor: أن الوصف ناظر إلى مدة الكون في النار أو الجنة من جهة النهاية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
rows.claim: A ninth view says the wretched remain in Hell during the world's duration, including their time in graves; when heaven and earth end, their torment pauses until resurrection, which is the exception.
rows.anchor: نقله في مجمع البيان عن شيخنا أبي جعفر الطوسي في تفسيره ناقلا عن جمع من أصحابنا في تفاسيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the ninth view restates the second view's reading of illa as 'other than' and inherits the objections raised against it.
rows.anchor: وفيه إن مرجعه إلى الوجه الثاني المبني على أخذ

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: A tenth view makes the first exception exclude people God pardons before they enter Hell; the Paradise exception then excludes sinful monotheists who enter Hell and later reach Paradise.
rows.anchor: ونسب الوجه إلى أبي مجلز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed account fits only the first exception and requires a different explanation for the second, breaking the two verses' contextual unity.
rows.anchor: وفيه إن ما ذكره إنما يجري في أول الاستثناءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People God pardons are not arbitrarily excused: pardon rests on a good deed or intercession, making them happy from the outset and included in Paradise's group, not wretches who must be excepted.
rows.anchor: هم ليسوا بأشقياء حتى يستثنوا بل سعداء داخلون في الجنة من أول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is read with سعدوا passive or active; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the active form because سعد is normally intransitive in Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: قرئ سعدوا بالبناء للمجهول وبالبناء للمعلوم والثاني أوفق باللغة لأن مادة سعد لازمة في المعروف من استعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading subtly suggests that happiness and good come from God, whereas the evil attached to people comes from themselves, as 24:21 says.
rows.anchor: لكن الأول وهو سعدوا بالبناء للمجهول مع كون

words: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's statement that no one would be purified without God's favor supports the allusion that good and happiness originate with God.
rows.anchor: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا النور 21

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadh means cutting; ʿaṭāʾ ghayr majdūdh therefore means a gift that is not cut off.
rows.anchor: والجذ هو القطع وعطاء غير مجذوذ أي غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Paradise an unsevered gift despite the exception supports al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī's reading: the will clause affirms God's unrestricted power and continuing ownership of the matter.
rows.anchor: وعده تعالى الجنة عطاء غير مجذوذ مع سبق الاستثناء من الخلود بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier interpretations based on moving people from Hell to Paradise cannot explain Paradise's exception: no one who enters the afterlife's Garden ever leaves it, as Quran and Sunna establish abundantly; Quranic evidence for some leaving Hell is less explicit.
rows.anchor: من الجائز أن يخرج من نار الآخرة بعض من دخله لكن لا يخرج من جنة الآخرة وهي جنة الخلد أحد ممن دخلها جزاء أبدا

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān reports community consensus that those deserving reward must enter Paradise and cannot leave after entry.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان في وجوب دخول أهل الطاعة الجنة وعدم جواز خروجهم منها لإجماع الأمة على أن من استحق الثواب فلا بد أن يدخل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to fulfill a promise follows a rational rule: withholding a promised right is injustice; punishment under a threat is God's own right, which He may enforce or waive, so He must reward the obedient but may forgive sinners.
rows.anchor: قاعدة عقلية مسلمة وهي أن الوفاء بالوعد واجب دون الوفاء بالوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consensus about entry and permanence in Paradise is not independent proof; it rests on the Quran, Sunna, or reason accepted by the community.
rows.anchor: والإجماع الذي ذكره مبني على الذي تسلموه من دلالة الكتاب والسنة أو العقل على ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet saying God gives a wrongdoer respite, then seizes him and does not let him escape; al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasaʾi, Ibn Majah, and others transmit it.
rows.anchor: إن الله سبحانه ليملي للظالم حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: After 11:105 was revealed, ʿUmar asked the Prophet whether deeds concern a matter already decided; the Prophet said it was decided and the pens had flowed, yet each person is facilitated for what they were created for. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال لما نزلت { فمنهم شقي وسعيد }

rows.speaker: عمران بن الحصين
rows.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, ʿImran ibn Husayn asks the Prophet what people work toward; he answers that each is facilitated for what they were created for.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن الحصين قال قلت يا رسول الله فيم يعمل العاملون

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says everyone's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands them to work, says each is facilitated for their creation, and recites 92:5.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before an event becomes actual, it remains possible relative to both existence and nonexistence; wood may become ash or not, and semen may become a human if the remaining causes join or may instead be extinguished.
rows.anchor: أن كلا من الحوادث الجارية في هذا العالم من أعيان وآثارها ما لم يلبس لباس التحقق والوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once an object becomes actual, its former alternatives cease: actual ash cannot simultaneously be unburned wood, and an actual human cannot remain nonhuman.
rows.anchor: وصار إنسانا فحسب يمتنع غيره ورمادا يمتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world can be viewed both as a necessary chain of actual causes and as a field of possibilities and dispositions before outcomes occur.
rows.anchor: فللكون وجهان وجه ضرورة فعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the possible, not-yet-realized perspective, choice, effort, education, hope and fear, commands, and reward and punishment have their proper place.
rows.anchor: وعليه يقوم ناموس الاختيار، وبه يتقوم السعي والحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first perspective is divine decree: events are determined through their causes, but that determination does not cancel their lack of determination in the domain of action and acquisition.
rows.anchor: والوجه الأول هو وجه القضاء الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Determined outcomes under decree do not negate the open-ended conditions that belong to the sphere of invitation, work, and acquisition.
rows.anchor: ولا يبطل تعين الحوادث بحسبه عدم تعينها بحسب ظرف الدعوة والعمل والاكتساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners inferred that a written destination makes deeds irrelevant and removes links between causes and outcomes, so someone destined for Paradise would reach it whether they acted well or badly.
rows.anchor: إذا قضي للإنسان بالجنة تحتم له ذلك سواء عمل أو لم يعمل وسواء عمل صالحا أو اقترف سيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also worried that the means themselves were fixed, leaving no room for choice or effort; their questions chiefly reveal the first inference, though the errors are connected.
rows.anchor: وكأن الذي كانوا يشاهدونه في أنفسهم من صفة الاختيار والاستطاعة صرفهم عن الإشارة إلى ثاني التوهمين وإن كان ناشبا على قلوبهم فإنهما متلازمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's answer means God makes the path to each person's created end accessible, as expressed by 80:20 and 7:179.
rows.anchor: أي إن كلا من أهل الجنة الذي خلقه الله لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The route to Paradise is faith and piety, and the route to Hell is polytheism and sin; the destination was not decreed apart from its required conduct.
rows.anchor: وسبيل الجنة هو الإيمان والتقوى، وسبيل النار هو الشرك والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defers a fuller treatment of divine decree and destiny to a later appropriate passage.
rows.anchor: وسنستوفي البحث في ذلك عندما نضع الكلام في القضاء والقدر فيما يناسبه من الموضع إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet answers the question about destiny: each person is facilitated for what they were created for.
rows.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In ʿAli's narration, the Prophet follows this answer with 92:5–10, describing ease toward good for those who give and fear God, and hardship for those who withhold and deny.
rows.anchor: فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى وأما من بخل واستغنى وكذب بالحسنى فنيسره للعسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cannot expect an end without following its path: this world is a place of effort and movement, and a person receives according to what they strive for, as 53:39–41 says.
rows.anchor: فالمتوقع لإحدى الغايتين من غير طريقه كالطامع في الشبع من غير أكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facilitation presupposes a matter that is not necessary or inevitable; otherwise easing the path would have no meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن التسهيل إنما يتحقق في أمر لا ضرورة تحتمه ولا وجوب يعينه ويسد باب عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith preserves two aspects of a person's outcome: necessary decree and possible choice through work; divine invitations address the latter aspect.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن لما يؤول إليه أمر الإنسان من السعادة والشقاء وجهين وجه ضرورة وقضاء حتم لا يتغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī points to his earlier discussion of free will while interpreting 2:26.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم كلام في الجبر والاختيار في تفسير قوله

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Qatada recited 11:106 and reported from Anas that the Prophet said a group will emerge from Hell.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، أنه تلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada added that they do not say what the people of Haruraʾ say; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī identifies the Harurites as Kharijites who claim whoever enters Hell remains there forever.
rows.anchor: ولا نقول كما قال أهل حروراء

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that after reciting the wretched people's passage through the exception, the Prophet said that if God wills to take some of them from Hell and put them in Paradise, He can.
rows.anchor: إن شاء الله أن يخرج أناسا من الذين شقوا من النار فيدخلهم الجنة فعل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In al-Burhan, Muhammad ibn Muslim asks Imam al-Sadiq about the Jahannamiyyun; Abu Jaʿfar says they leave Hell, reach the spring of life at Paradise's gate, and regrow after its water is sprinkled on them. A parallel transmission comes through ʿUmar ibn Aban.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن الجهنميين فقال كان أبو جعفر يقول يخرجون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannamiyyun are a particular group of Hell's inhabitants: monotheists released through intercession, not all who enter Hell.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالجهنميين طائفة خاصة من أهل النار وهم أهل التوحيد الخارجون منها بالشفاعة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar tells Abu Basir that some become charcoal in Hell before intercession takes them to a river from Paradise's spring; bathing restores their flesh and removes the fire's grime, and Paradise's people call them Jahannamiyyun until God removes that name.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول إن أناسا يخرجون من النار

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the enemies of ʿAli remain in Hell forever and intercession does not reach them.
rows.anchor: يا أبا بصير إن أعداء علي هم المخلدون في النار ولا تدركهم الشفاعة

rows.speaker: عبد صالح
rows.claim: A righteous servant says Jahannamiyyun enter Hell for their sins and leave through God's pardon.
rows.anchor: قال سمعت عبدا صالحا يقول في الجهنميين إنهم يدخلون النار بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Answering Humran's objection to people leaving Hell for Paradise, Imam al-Sadiq cites 55:62: there are gardens below gardens and fires below fires, and the rescued group does not live alongside God's close servants.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام إنهم يقولون لا تعجبون من قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam says a station lies between these groups but cannot explain it; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the Qaʾim will begin with the scoffers when he rises, as retribution.
rows.anchor: أي إذا ظهر بدأ بهؤلاء المستهزئين بأهل الحق انتقاما

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In al-ʿAyyashi's Tafsir, Humran asks Abu Jaʿfar about the exception in the abiding clause; he says it refers to those who leave the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن حمران عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Jaʿfar's distinction: the exception is stated for Hell's people but, for Paradise's people, the clause is followed by 'an unsevered gift.'
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains that the Paradise exception, followed by an unsevered gift, does not remove anyone; it asserts unrestricted power, unlike Hell's exception followed by 'your Lord does what He wills,' which suggests an actual release.
rows.anchor: يشير عليه السلام إلى أن الاستثناء بالمشيئة في أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says both clauses were later abrogated: a Medinan threat removed hope that Hell's people would leave, while a promise to believers established Paradise's eternal duration.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن السدي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects al-Suddi's abrogation claim: it assumes the verses imply eventual termination, lacks rational or transmitted basis, conflicts with explicit Paradise wording, and ignores other Meccan declarations of both groups' abiding.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره من نسخ الآيتين زعما منه أنهما تدلان على الانقطاع

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Hasan reports that ʿUmar said that even if Hell's people stayed as long as a heap of sand at ʿAlij, a day would come when they left.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن عن عمر قال لو لبث أهل النار في النار كقدر رمل عالج لكان لهم يوم على ذلك يخرجون فيه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says a day will come when no one remains in Hell, and he recited 11:106.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال سيأتي على جهنم يوم لا يبقى فيها أحد

words: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك
rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says no Quran verse gives Hell's people greater hope than 11:107.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال ما في القرآن آية أرجى لأهل النار من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibrahim also attributes to Ibn Masʿud the claim that a time will come when Hell's doors flap with no one left inside.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ليأتين عليها زمان تخفق أبوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says these Companion statements do not bind others; even as suspended reports they are rejected for contradicting the Quran's statement that disbelievers will not leave the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولو فرضت روايات موقوفة لكانت مطروحة بمخالفة الكتاب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Humran reports that Imam al-Sadiq rejects the claim that Hell's doors will one day shut empty, insisting on eternal duration; he explains 11:107 as referring to those who leave Hell.
rows.anchor: عن حمران قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام إنه بلغنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports from the Imami Imams establish disbelievers' eternal punishment; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī previously discussed whether punishment can end in his commentary on 2:167.
rows.anchor: والروايات الدالة على خلود الكفار في النار من طرق أئمة أهل البيت كثيرة جدا
